question: Waterproof laminate vs luxury vinyl plank: which is better in Florida humidity?
title: Waterproof Laminate vs Luxury Vinyl Plank in Florida
h1: Which Is Better in Florida Humidity, Waterproof Laminate or LVP?
description: This Old House prices laminate at $5-$12/sq ft and vinyl plank at $5-$20/sq ft installed. See which handles Sarasota-area humidity better in 2026.
capsule: Waterproof laminate and luxury vinyl plank cost about the same — This Old House puts laminate installed at $5-$12/sq ft and vinyl plank at $5-$20/sq ft. Their warranties differ more: Pergo's WetProtect laminate covers spills and pet accidents but excludes flooding and standing water. Our verdict: LVP is the safer pick near Sarasota-area kitchens, bathrooms and lanais; laminate works fine in drier living spaces.

sections.h2: Which Is Better in Florida Humidity, Waterproof Laminate or LVP?
sections.html:
Priced side by side, the two aren't far apart. This Old House's national cost data puts laminate installed at roughly $5-$12 per sq ft and vinyl plank at $5-$20 per sq ft depending on grade, so cost alone rarely decides it for a Sarasota-area remodel, and most of our clients end up choosing based on room use rather than sticking to a strict budget line. What decides it, most of the time, is what a warranty actually protects against. Water-resistant laminate like Pergo's WetProtect line covers household spills, pet accidents and wet mopping, which is most of daily life. It specifically excludes flooding, standing water, leaking pipes and appliance leaks, the categories more likely to hit a Gulf Coast home than an inland one. Reading that exclusion list before ordering material is worth the five minutes it takes, since it is usually the part of the warranty homeowners skip past.

Both materials also handle the visual side of things well; modern printing technology means a laminate or vinyl plank can convincingly mimic wide-plank white oak or hickory from a few feet away, so the choice increasingly comes down to performance in specific rooms rather than looks. If real wood is still what you're after, our guide to the best flooring for a Florida home covers where engineered hardwood fits into that comparison instead.

sections.h2: Laminate vs LVP, Side by Side
sections.html:
Water-resistant laminateWaterproof LVP/SPC
Core materialCompressed wood fiber, sealed edgesStone or wood-plastic composite, rigid
Typical installed cost (national, 2026)$5–$12/sq ft$5–$20/sq ft
What the warranty coversSpills, pet accidents, wet moppingEveryday moisture, most spills
What it excludesFlooding, standing water, leaksVaries; slab moisture limits still apply

In an air-conditioned bedroom, office or living room that never sees standing water, water-resistant laminate holds up well and often has a warmer, more wood-like look for less money than a comparable engineered hardwood. We install it in plenty of Sarasota and Manatee County homes for exactly those rooms, with a proper moisture barrier under it on any slab. It's also a reasonable pick for a second-story room over a wood subfloor, where slab moisture isn't part of the equation at all. Owners who like the slightly warmer, softer feel of laminate over a foam underlayment often choose it for a primary bedroom for that reason alone, even when budget isn't the deciding factor. A home office or a guest room that rarely sees foot traffic at all is another easy yes for laminate in this climate.

Kitchens, bathrooms, laundry rooms and lanai transitions are where the gap widens. LVP's rigid core and sealed seams handle standing water and repeated wet mopping better over years, even though neither material is a flood solution once water actually breaches the surface and reaches the subfloor underneath. See our waterproof flooring guide for the full rundown of how each material actually performs in a wet room, or run your room list through our Florida flooring finder tool to get a material recommendation by room. Many of our clients end up with a mixed spec, laminate in the bedrooms and office, LVP everywhere water is a realistic daily risk, rather than picking one material for the whole house. A written, line-itemized quote makes that kind of room-by-room mix easy to compare side by side before you commit to either product.

faqs.q: Is waterproof laminate a real thing, or just marketing?
faqs.a: It's real in the sense that products like Pergo WetProtect carry a specific warranty against spills and pet accidents, but it's not the same standard as a fully waterproof vinyl core. Read the excluded-events list before assuming full flood protection.

faqs.q: Which one is quieter underfoot, laminate or LVP?
faqs.a: Laminate over a foam underlayment is often slightly quieter and warmer feeling than rigid-core LVP, which is one reason some owners still choose it for bedrooms.

faqs.q: Does either one need a moisture barrier over a concrete slab?
faqs.a: Laminate always does per Mohawk's installation guidance. LVP's requirement depends on the specific product; see our post on moisture barriers under vinyl plank on a concrete slab.
